elements.id-string-14: This study introduces the P5 model - a foundational method that utilizes reinforcement learning (RL) to augment control, effectiveness, and scalability in molecular dynamics simulations (MD).
elements.id-string-15: Our innovative strategy optimizes the sampling of target polymer chain conformations, marking an efficiency improvement of over $37.1\%$.
elements.id-string-16: The RL-induced control policies function as an inductive bias, modulating Brownian forces to steer the system towards the preferred state, thereby expanding the exploration of the configuration space beyond what traditional MD allows.
elements.id-string-17: This broadened exploration generates a more varied set of conformations and targets specific properties, a feature pivotal for progress in polymer development, drug discovery, and material design.
elements.id-string-18: Our technique offers significant advantages when investigating new systems with limited prior knowledge, opening up new methodologies for tackling complex simulation problems with generative techniques.

elements.id-string-22: Molecular dynamics has emerged as an invaluable tool for examining molecular systems, albeit with certain limitations.
elements.id-string-23: These methods often prove computationally intensive, particularly when handling complex systems such as macromolecules, for instance, polymer chains with more than $10^4$ atoms.
elements.id-string-24: In addition, uncertainties may arise due to this increasing system complexity, inaccuracies in complex definitions such as force fields, or limited knowledge about de Novo molecular systems.
elements.id-string-25: Machine learning has shown promise in addressing these challenges with data-driven methods like property predictions using discriminative techniques \cite{karuth_predicting_2021, tao_benchmarking_2021}, and machine learning force fields \cite{doerr_torchmd_2021, kleinschmidt_computational_2022, unke_machine_2021}.
elements.id-string-26: Computational chemistry has seen machine learning techniques gradually incorporate 3D \cite{ganea_geomol_2021} and graph representations \cite{antoniuk_representing_2022, park_prediction_2022, you_graph_2018, zuo_accelerating_2021}.
elements.id-string-27: Recent work has included physics analysis to inform generative molecular machine learning \cite{liu_genphys_2023}.
elements.id-string-28: Despite these advances, deriving molecular properties that demand expectations over an ensemble of states or time-dependent behavior of atoms and molecules remains relatively unexplored.
elements.id-string-29: This paper presents P5, an RL-based control policy system in a three-dimensional physics engine simulator to enhance molecular simulation processes.
elements.id-string-30: P5 stands for Predicting Polymer Properties and Processability with Physics-Informed Reinforcement Learning.
elements.id-string-31: By utilizing reinforcement learning with a molecular dynamics module, including Brownian Dynamics, we extend the scope of application for control policies in molecular dynamics simulations.
elements.id-string-32: Our approach demonstrated increased control over uncertainty and addressed previous limitations in modeling and manipulating the polymer chain's structural dynamics.
elements.id-string-33: Our work builds upon existing molecular dynamics sampling machine learning algorithms.
elements.id-string-34: While \citet{holdijk_path_2022} demonstrate how a physics-inspired approach for transition sampling may provide direct control over molecular systems, P5's RL approach offers flexibility, adaptability, and environmental feedback.
elements.id-string-35: \citet{klein_timewarp_2023} introduce 'TimeWarp,' which utilizes the Metropolis-Hastings algorithm for probabilistic sampling, while P5 actively targets specific states.
elements.id-string-36: Rose et al. \cite{rose_reinforcement_2021} deploy RL to sample rare events in their molecular dynamics research and P5 seeks an array of targets.
elements.id-string-37: Our approach focuses on increasing control and efficiency over macromolecule dynamics.
elements.id-string-38: Furthermore, it builds upon RL extensive applications in robotics through training on 3D physics engines \cite{muratore_robot_2022, brockman_openai_2016, todorov_mujoco_2012, juliani_unity_2020}, which are widely used for model-based control learning.
elements.id-string-39: Reinforcement learning algorithms, notably A3C \cite{mnih_asynchronous_2016} and PPO \cite{schulman_proximal_2017}, form the foundation of these platforms, driving control systems for kinetic simulators.
elements.id-string-40: Through simulating a molecule of Cellulose Acetate (renewable biopolymer chain) with P5, we demonstrate how RL-based control policies offer improved exploration of the configuration space, adaptation to specific objectives, and optimization of computational resources in over a $37.1\%$  improvement of polymer chain conformation sampling targeting a known radius of gyration range.
elements.id-string-41: This approach boosts the efficiency of the simulation process and fosters the development of RL-based control policies, which enhance the precision and efficiency of the simulations.
elements.id-string-42: Furthermore, P5 can be extended to various molecular systems, underscoring its transferability to de Novo molecules, applicability to cross-scale problems, and generating new conformations.
elements.id-string-43: The P5 model development with inexpensive computation and data makes P5 a promising tool for accelerating polymer research and development.
elements.id-string-44: Furthermore, this simulation technology advancement can accelerate discoveries in various scientific and engineering domains.
elements.id-string-47: We introduced P5, a generative simulator developed to predict polymer properties and processing using physics-informed reinforcement learning to advance molecular dynamics simulations.
elements.id-string-48: This system was built on Unity 3D, a physics game engine that allows for the simulation of Newtonian physics of motion and 3D geometric representation of chemical structures.
elements.id-string-49: We incorporated the ML-agents module within the Unity environment, including standard reinforcement learning algorithms, Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) \cite{schulman_proximal_2017}, and other similar techniques.
elements.id-string-50: We selected PPO as our reinforcement learning algorithm due to its flexibility and balanced exploration-exploitation trade-off.
elements.id-string-51: We 'froze' the components of the MD, 3D-physics, RL, and the molecular system, thus concentrating our efforts on designing control policies for molecular dynamics\footnote{See Appendix 1, including error detection.}.
elements.id-string-52: Our simulation framework incorporated the extensively-validated Martini Force Field \cite{bereau_automated_2015} for representing organic molecules explained in Appendix 3.
elements.id-string-53: The geometric modeling of P5 is performed in Unity, with hinge joints employed to emulate bonds between polymer chain beads, facilitating precise rotational dynamics and an accurate depiction of the structural intricacies of the polymer chain.
elements.id-string-54: We utilized SMILE and Gromacs readers for monomer topology, enabling precise bead position retrieval in Cartesian space using RDKit \cite{landrum_rdkit_2010}.
elements.id-string-55: The nonbonded interactions were modeled through Lennard-Jones and Brownian forces as an implicit solvent.
elements.id-string-56: Collectively, these methodologies contribute to a high-fidelity representation of polymeric molecular systems.
elements.id-string-57: In the P5 model, the operational timescale is denoted as a dimensionless timestep, attributable to its implementation in the physics engine.
elements.id-string-58: This dimensionless timestep can be converted to physical time units such as femtoseconds using characteristic values of the relevant properties (e.g., bond lengths, bond angles, atomic masses) to derive the appropriate scaling factor.
elements.id-string-59: The selection of the exact scaling factor is contingent on the specific system under study and forms a crucial part of the model calibration process \footnote{See Appendix 2.}.
elements.id-string-60: The development and training phase of the P5 model was conducted on a standard laptop, demonstrating its compatibility with commonly accessible computing resources.
elements.id-string-61: However, the model can be executed on cloud computing platforms for increased performance by 10x and scalability.
elements.id-string-63: The control policy is optimized by a neural network (NN) agent that manipulates Brownian forces acting on the backbone beads of the polymer chain (PC).
elements.id-string-64: This process propels the beads to swiftly alter their positions, enabling a transition from an initial conformation to a target ensemble defined by a pre-specified radius of gyration (RG) range.

elements.id-string-66: The Dynamics component, $S_{\text{dynamics}}$, captures the position $r_s$, velocity $v_s$, and angular velocity $w_s$ of the rigid body of the beads.
elements.id-string-67: The Environmental component, $S_{\text{environment}}$, reflects the positions of other neighboring beads' rigid bodies, encapsulated in the set $others_s$, within a specific observation radius around the current rigid body, to provide environmental feedback.
